Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: isolated newspaper front-page style sample for Scene 1 of a 2.5D wartime animation. Style: Non-realistic 2.5D wartime illustration with a simplified low-poly appearance. Use broad angular planes, clean polygonal silhouettes, restrained human proportions and economical facial features. Apply muted olive, khaki, grey-green, earth brown and subdued warm skin tones. Materials are matte, with sparse texture and two or three broad shading tones. Keep outlines subtle and helmet shadows simple. Build depth through overlapping, separately layered foreground, middle-ground and background artwork. Preserve each character’s silhouette, costume and proportions across poses. Keep the mood quiet, human and sombre.
Subject: one open newspaper facing the reader nearly straight on, entirely visible, slightly angular paper edges and subtle central fold. Cream newsprint in broad flat tones, sparse texture, no dense faceting, matte. The top-right corner is only slightly curled. Genuine transparent background; no hands, furniture, other props, border, floor or shadows outside the paper.
Exact front-page text: masthead "The Front Line Gazette"; dateline "Sunday, December 17, 1944"; large headline "ALLIES PUSH ON"; immediately below it the subheadline "‘BOYS HOME BY CHRISTMAS,’ SAYS GENERAL". Spell these exactly. Use black newspaper serif type with clear hierarchy, enough blank margin for newspaper grip at both sides. The headline must remain legible. Below use quiet narrow column rules and subtle unreadable print marks, not invented legible news, names or casualty counts. Reserve a modest blank section for the later casualty-list overlay because its wording is not specified. No photos or unrelated illustration. Wide image, neutral diffuse lighting, colour base art rather than a baked whole-screen halftone effect. Only ONE front-page view; not a multi-state sheet.
